name: Mattaniah
overview: Mattaniah is a male biblical figure identified as a descendant of Bani. His notable attribute is that he had married a foreign wife, a fact recorded in the book of Ezra. There is no further tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Mattaniah means 'gift of YHWH,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the Lord. This proper name is mentioned explicitly in Ezra 10:37 and does not indicate that it was given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Mattaniah as a descendant of Bani, establishing a familial link within that lineage. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Mattaniah's significance in the biblical narrative arises from his inclusion among those who had taken foreign wives during the post-exilic period, as noted in Ezra 10:37. This detail highlights the community's struggle with maintaining covenantal purity and obedience to God's commands after the return from exile. His example serves as a reminder of the challenges faced by Israel in upholding holiness and faithfulness to the Lord.
